text:
Alex: Heads up — ran into a weird p99 regression when we enable lazy-evict + prefill on the same prefix. Can we sync on handshake semantics?
Jamie: ugh, that combo's been gnarly. Any logs or sequence you can paste?
Alex: minimal reproduction: tenant hot, partial prefill kicks in, then lazy-evict starts a soft-demote handshake, but prefill workers try to rehydrate concurrently. Result: double-inflight and latency spike.
Pat: are the prefill workers checking an ownership token before streaming back KV chunks?
Alex: currently they only check eviction flag in metadata. No strong token CAS. That's probably the root.
Sara: thinking aloud: we need an explicit prefill admission that respects the soft-demote -> demote-ack contract. Otherwise we get flapping.
Kevin: +1. Two approaches: (1) make prefill idempotent and cancelable (best-effort, safe to ignore late chunks) or (2) strengthen handshake with an epoch token that prefill must fetch before sending chunks.
Jamie: option 1 is less invasive but will complicate bookkeeping. Option 2 adds a small RPC but is clearer semantically.
Alex: here's a sketch for option 2: prefill flow -> fetch_epoch(prefix) -> returns {epoch, lease_id} -> prefill starts; evict path compares epoch and either accepts or rejects. If mismatch, prefill aborts and drops data.
Alex: code example: ```json
POST /prefill/start
body: { prefix: "p/x", worker_id: "w-12" }
resp: { epoch: 12345, lease: "l-abc" }
```
Pat: what about the timing window where an evict starts after fetch_epoch but before chunk upload finishes? We still need server-side gate at apply-time.
Sara: exactly — server must recheck epoch when applying chunks and reject if epoch changed. That keeps correctness.
Kevin: rejection path needs to be cheap; we don't want full-compaction on every reject. Maybe return a soft-retry hint: backoff_ms or preferred-node.
Jamie: UX for prefill workers: on reject, they do exponential backoff, optionally fetch latest epoch and retry only if epoch matches and eviction state is not demoted.
Alex: another trade: what about partial-accept? If some chunks arrive and then eviction completes, applying subset could leave inconsistent residency. So server must apply atomically per prefill session or reject whole session.
Pat: atomic apply per session seems right. We already have session ids for big uploads; reuse that.
Sara: ops question — can we detect pathological tenants who cause repeated prefill->evict churn and throttle them?
Kevin: yes, add a tenant backoff counter and throttle prefill attempts for X seconds after N rejects. Keeps workers from thrashing.
Alex: one more: metrics. We need counters for prefill_attempts, prefill_rejects_by_epoch, prefill_retries_throttled. Also histogram for prefill_apply_duration.
Jamie: agreed. Also add a labeled counter for reject_reason (epoch_mismatch, demoted, quota).
evict-bot: Note: deploy scheduled for next canary on pref/test at 2026-04-02T03:00Z :gear:
Pat: implementation plan I propose: 
  - API: add /prefill/start returning epoch + session_id
  - Server: gate apply by epoch+session atomically
  - Worker: on reject, consult backoff policy and only retry if epoch advanced
  - Metrics + throttles
Sara: timeline? can we do a spike and small prototype in a week?
Alex: I can spike the server gate and metrics this week. Jamie, can you help with worker changes and test harness?
Jamie: yup. I'll mock failure paths in the harness and add e2e where prefill races an explicit evict.
Kevin: we'll also add a small load test to validate p99 under mixed prefill+evict patterns.
Alex: ok — action items:
  - Alex: server gate + metrics spike (this week)
  - Jamie: worker retry/backoff + harness tests (this week)
  - Pat: design review of session atomic apply (tomorrow)
  - Sara: add throttling proposal to infra board (Fri)
  - Kevin: load test scenarios + thresholds (next week)
Sara: ping me when the spike is up, I'll try to break it. :mag: :boom:
Alex: thanks all. If anyone has objections to the epoch/session approach speak up now. Otherwise I'll open a tiny RFC and a draft PR.
Kevin: no objections from me. Seems like the most correct tradeoff. :+1:
Jamie: sounds good.
Pat: lgtm.
Alex: I'll open thread PR link when ready.
Alex: (follow-up) one last nuance — should prefill sessions carry a manifest checksum so server can assert all chunks belong to the same prefill? That avoids partial-mix with other sessions.
Pat: yes, session checksum is cheap and adds safety.
Alex: cool — I'll include that in the PR.
Alex: thanks everyone!
